scope.description: Specification-level threat model of shrink-182, a team link shortener, before any code exists. Web is the primary architecture; API is a bounded secondary for the JSON API. Revision r06 reviews the specification change 10b7ddf..e8e2b87 against baseline r05.
in_scope: Fastify HTTP layer and JSON API (session cookie and bearer token)
Auth, Links, Redirect, Admin and Account deletion modules
Configuration, SQLite store, security event file
out_of_scope: Host OS, GitHub repository settings and CI
A hosted deployment (only a localhost demo is specified)
Supply-chain architecture analysis beyond what the web and API lenses touch
objectives: Find design-level threats in the specifications
Give supported findings stable T-nnn IDs so they can be folded back into the specs
Leave a JSON baseline for later change reviews
assumptions: The five specification documents at revision 10b7ddf are the intended design
The demo runs on a developer machine at http://localhost, as ARCHITECTURE.md states
limitations: Nothing is implemented; every statement about a control describes a design, not behavior
No risk rubric, prior model, method fragment or secure-coding pack was supplied
Working-tree cleanliness was not checked with Git because of the runbook's filter rule
Absent surfaces are recorded as not applicable: uploads, payments, shared caches, third-party resources, background jobs, callbacks, federation, multi-tenancy
The system model is reconstructed from specification text and diagrams only; elements have basis proposed_design
Threats are grounded design hypotheses about the specifications; none is an evidenced weakness, and none is rated
Challenge was done against the wording of the specifications only; no control could be confirmed or defeated by observation
Treatments are proposals, verification plans are not_run, risks are unrated and decisions have no owner or date

threats.scenario: A page from another origin makes the signed-in user's browser send a state-changing request (create, edit or delete a link, revoke a token, delete the account, an admin delete) that the server accepts on the strength of the session cookie alone.
threats.objective: Integrity of the user's links, tokens and account; for an admin, of every user's links and accounts.
prerequisites: The victim has a valid session
The victim opens an attacker-controlled page in the same browser
The fetch-metadata/Origin and content-type check is missing or bypassable on the targeted route
actor_assumptions: Can host a web page and get the victim to open it
Cannot read the session cookie
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: SC-015 now also covers ceremony routes and runs before rate limiting. Its new sentence exempting 'bearer-token routes' is ambiguous for link routes that accept either credential (G-020). Still a designed control only.

threats.scenario: Sign-up and login routes are not authenticated by the session cookie, so the wording of SC-015 does not cover them. A cross-site page submits a login completion for the attacker's own account, or a second party completes a ceremony against a challenge issued to someone else. The victim ends up signed in as the attacker and saves links (target URLs) into the attacker's account.
threats.objective: Confidentiality of URLs the victim shortens; integrity of which account a browser is signed in to.
prerequisites: The ceremony routes accept a cross-site request
A challenge is not tied to the browser that requested it, or can be used twice under concurrent requests
The attacker has their own registered passkey
actor_assumptions: Can host a web page and get the victim to open it
Holds a valid account and passkey
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: SC-015 now gates sign-up and login, and SC-011 binds each challenge to the requesting browser and deletes it before verifying. Both premises are addressed in the design. Open until implemented and tested (V-002).

threats.scenario: Sign-up and login are limited to 10 attempts per minute per socket address. On the localhost demo every browser tab and local process shares the loopback address, and the ceremony routes are reachable cross-site. Any page the user visits, or any local process, can spend the allowance and keep the user locked out of login.
prerequisites: Ceremony option or verify requests count against the limit before any origin check
The attacker's requests arrive from the same socket address as the user's
actor_assumptions: Can host a web page the user opens, or run a process on the same host or behind the same address
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: cross-site requests are refused before they count (SC-015), foreign Host names are refused (SC-026) and the server listens only on loopback (SC-032). A local process on the same machine can still spend the allowance; that is inherent to an address key. Confidence lowered from medium.

threats.scenario: Admin authority is granted to whoever holds an internal user ID listed in configuration. The specs do not say how IDs are generated or that they are never reused. If IDs are sequential or reusable, a new sign-up can receive an ID that is still in the admin list after the original admin account was deleted, and becomes an admin. Reuse would also mis-attribute retained security events.
threats.objective: Admin authority (TB-4): every user's links and accounts; attribution in the event file.
prerequisites: An ID in the admin list no longer belongs to the intended person (the account was deleted, or the ID was listed in advance)
A new account can obtain that ID
actor_assumptions: Can sign up (sign-up is open to anyone who reaches the site)
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: FR-7.9 and SC-027 require random, never-reused IDs and report unmatched admin entries; FR-7.10 stops admins deleting themselves. The premise now fails by design. Confidence lowered from medium. Open until implemented (V-004).

threats.scenario: One JSON API accepts a session cookie or a bearer token, but the specs do not list which routes accept which. A leaked or over-shared API token could reach account, passkey, token-management or admin routes, and a request carrying both credentials could be checked under one and acted on under the other.
threats.objective: Limit of a token's authority to link management; integrity of account and admin functions.
prerequisites: A token is obtained by someone other than its owner, or a request carries both a cookie and a token
A non-link route accepts the bearer credential, or the CSRF check is skipped when an Authorization header is present
actor_assumptions: Holds a valid API token, their own or a leaked one
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: FR-5.9, SC-028 and the route map limit tokens to link routes and refuse mixed credentials. Confidence lowered from medium. Open until implemented (V-005).

threats.scenario: A signed-in user or API client changes the short code in a view, edit or delete call to reach a link owned by someone else, or calls an admin route without the admin role. The admin list-all route is the one bulk path; it returns every user's links and IDs.
threats.objective: Confidentiality and integrity of other users' links (TB-3); admin-only functions (TB-4).
prerequisites: The ownership filter or role check is missing on one route or one operation
Or a response returns fields beyond the allowed set
actor_assumptions: Has an account or a valid token
Knows or guesses a 7-character code
threats.confidence_rationale: SC-016 places the ownership check in the Links module for every read, edit and delete with a uniform not-found, and SC-021 limits response fields. Nothing is built. A two-account comparison across every operation, by cookie and by token, would decide it.

threats.scenario: A user stores a title or target URL crafted to be interpreted as markup or a live link. It is later shown in another user's context: the admin's list of all links, a delete-confirmation dialog that names the link and owner, or a tooltip. If interpreted, it runs with the admin's session.
threats.objective: Integrity of the admin's session and actions; TB-5.
prerequisites: User content reaches a sink that interprets it (HTML, a URL attribute) instead of text
The CSP does not stop the result
actor_assumptions: Has an account and can create links
threats.confidence_rationale: SC-009 (text only, no target in href) and SC-010 (CSP limited to 'self') are both specified and each would defeat it. Nothing is built. Rendering hostile titles and URLs in the admin list, the dialogs and the tooltip would decide it.

threats.scenario: A target URL is accepted and displayed in a form that misleads the reader about where it goes: a trusted-looking name before an @ sign, an internationalized look-alike host shown in Unicode, or a title containing direction-override or control characters that reorders what is displayed. DESIGN.md relies on the visible host to expose look-alike domains.
threats.objective: Users' and admins' ability to judge a link's destination from the list and from confirmation dialogs.
prerequisites: SC-003 accepts URLs with embedded credentials, or the display shows the submitted string instead of the parsed host
Or titles may contain control or direction-override characters
actor_assumptions: Has an account and can create links
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: FR-2.12 to FR-2.14 and SC-003 refuse embedded credentials and control characters and store the serialized URL. Confidence lowered from medium. Open until implemented (V-008).

threats.scenario: Sign-up is open and uncapped, and any http/https target is allowed. Anyone who can reach the site can create an account and use shrink-182 links as a trusted-looking front for phishing or malware destinations. Removal depends on an admin noticing.
threats.objective: Trust in links served from the team's short-link host; safety of visitors.
prerequisites: The site is reachable by people outside the team
No admin has removed the link or account
actor_assumptions: Can reach the site and register a passkey
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: NFR-1.4 and SC-032 keep the system on localhost, so outsiders cannot reach it. The scenario returns only if that rule is lifted. The answer is a proposed default (DEC-002).

threats.scenario: FR-2.10 rejects targets on the site's own domain, and SC-003 compares the target host with the configured site host. A target that names the same server another way (a different spelling of the loopback host, a trailing dot, another port on the same host) passes the comparison and lets links point back at the service, including at each other in a loop.
threats.objective: The FR-2.10 rule; availability for a visitor caught in a redirect loop; inflated click counts.
prerequisites: The own-host comparison is an exact string match against one configured name
actor_assumptions: Has an account and can create links
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: SC-003 now compares normalized host names and treats loopback names as the site. Confidence lowered from medium. Open until implemented (V-010).

threats.scenario: API rate limits are keyed by the hash of the presented token. A caller who sends a different random token on each request never reaches a limit. Each rejected request also writes an auth.api_token_rejected event, so the caller can fill the 10 MiB x 5 event file and rotate audit-required events out before the operator reads them.
threats.objective: Availability of the API; retention of audit evidence in the event file.
prerequisites: Requests with missing or unknown tokens are limited per token hash, or not at all
Rejection events are written without a volume bound
actor_assumptions: Can reach the API; needs no account
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: unknown-token calls are keyed by address (SC-018) and denial events have a ceiling (SC-025). The flush path is addressed in the design, but the ceiling itself opens T-018. Confidence lowered from medium.

threats.scenario: Every anonymous request for an existing short link performs a synchronous database write to count the click, and redirects are deliberately not rate-limited. A flood of redirect requests can occupy the single process and also inflate any link's click count.
threats.objective: Availability of the whole service (one event loop); integrity of click counts.
prerequisites: The attacker can send requests at a rate the process cannot absorb
actor_assumptions: Can reach the site; needs no account
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: SC-034 limits each redirect to one statement and NFR-1.5 records the flood risk as accepted for the demo. That acceptance is a proposed default, not a caller decision (DEC-004), and it does not remove the scenario.

threats.scenario: Short codes are the only thing protecting a link's target from anonymous readers. Someone guesses codes against the unlimited redirect route to harvest target URLs, which may include private document links.
prerequisites: Codes are predictable or drawn with bias, or the attacker can afford a very large number of requests
actor_assumptions: Can reach the site; needs no account
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: SC-029 requires a cryptographic source without bias. Open until implemented (V-013).

threats.scenario: Account deletion spans the Auth module (user, passkeys, sessions, tokens) and the Links module (links, retired codes). If it is not atomic, a failure midway leaves live links without an owner or tokens and sessions that still work for a deleted user, and a request already in flight may act for an account that is being deleted.
threats.objective: FR-1.11 and FR-5.8: a deleted account leaves no working link, token or session.
prerequisites: Deletion is done as separate steps without one transaction
A step fails or a concurrent request interleaves
actor_assumptions: Is the account owner or an admin; or simply a failure occurs
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: FR-1.12 and SC-030 require one transaction with full rollback. Open until implemented (V-014).

threats.scenario: Someone who briefly controls a signed-in browser (an unattended laptop, a stolen session) adds their own passkey. The session alone authorizes it. The owner cannot see or remove passkeys, so the intruder keeps access after the session ends; the only remedy is deleting the account. The same session can create an API token or delete the account.
prerequisites: The attacker can act within a valid session for a short time
actor_assumptions: Has temporary use of the victim's signed-in browser or session
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: FR-1.13 to FR-1.15 and SC-033 add passkey listing and removal and require a passkey assertion from the last 5 minutes for sensitive actions. Residual: someone who takes over a session within 5 minutes of the owner's own assertion can still add a passkey, and can then remove the owner's. Confidence lowered from medium.

threats.scenario: Authenticated JSON responses (the link list, the admin lists, the one-time token value) carry no cache directive. On a shared machine they may remain in the browser's cache or history after logout or session expiry.
threats.objective: Confidentiality of link data and of a freshly created API token after sign-out.
prerequisites: Another person uses the same browser profile after the user signs out
The browser stored the response
actor_assumptions: Has later access to the same browser profile
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: SC-031 requires no-store on every API response. Open until implemented (V-016).

threats.scenario: Several controls are justified only by the localhost demo: no TLS or HSTS, a Secure cookie that works because localhost is treated as secure, trustProxy off, rate limits keyed by socket address, no Host check. If the same build is put on a network or behind a proxy without revisiting them, the controls weaken silently: all clients may share one rate-limit key, cookies travel without TLS guarantees, and open sign-up meets real outsiders.
threats.objective: Effectiveness of the session, rate-limit and redirect-abuse controls outside the demo.
prerequisites: The system is deployed somewhere other than a developer's localhost
The localhost-only decisions are not revisited
actor_assumptions: Any network attacker or outside visitor, once the system is reachable
threats.confidence_rationale: Change reviewed: SC-032 refuses any origin but localhost, so the weakened-control condition cannot arise without a deliberate rule change. Proposed default (DEC-002).

threats.scenario: The new volume ceiling writes at most 60 denied or failure records per minute for each event name and only counts the rest. Someone first triggers 60 cheap denials of one event name (for example authorization denials or rejected input), then performs the probing they want hidden in the same minute. Those later records are counted but not written, so the operator cannot see who did what.
threats.objective: Accountability: per-event detail (actor, route, reason) for denied and failed actions in the event file.
prerequisites: The ceiling is shared by all callers for one event name
The attacker can cause 60 denials of that event name within a minute
actor_assumptions: Can reach the API; an account or token is needed only for events that require one
threats.confidence_rationale: Supported by the wording of SC-025 and the event contract: one ceiling per event name, not per actor or reason. Against it: suppressed events are still counted in logging.health, audit-required events are exempt, and rate limits bound token callers to 60 calls a minute. A ceiling that never suppresses records carrying an identified actor would defeat it.

requirements.statement: No account recovery path exists.
A logged-in user can delete their own account; their links are deleted and answer not-found.
A target URL on shrink-182's own domain is rejected.
No visitor-identifying data is stored when a link is followed.
Every request for an existing short link counts as one click, with no filtering.
Missing and not-owned links give the same not-found response.
The JSON API identifies the caller by API token and acts as its owner.
The admin role is assigned only in deployment configuration.
Sign-up and login limited to 10 per minute per network address; API to 60 per minute per token; redirects not limited.
Internal user IDs are never reused, including after account deletion. (T-004)

requirements.statement: A user can remove a passkey, except the last one.
Adding or removing a passkey, creating an API token and deleting one's own account need a passkey authentication from the last 5 minutes.
An admin cannot delete their own account by any route while their ID is in the admin configuration.
The system runs only at http://localhost and refuses any other origin.
Unlimited short-link traffic is accepted for the localhost demo.

T-001: Challenged: SC-015 would be defeated by a route that changes state on GET, by a body parser that accepts a non-JSON content type, or by the check running after the handler. Its wording rules out the first two for cookie-authenticated routes; nothing observed rules out the third (G-019). SameSite=Lax is a second barrier for cross-site POSTs. Stays open at low confidence until tested.

T-002: Challenged: a preflight requirement would stop a cross-site JSON POST only if the ceremony routes refuse other content types, which SC-015 does not require of them. A single-use challenge does not by itself tie the ceremony to one browser. The premise stands; the practical path is narrow. Stays open at low confidence.

T-003: Challenged: looked for a specified protection that keeps another origin's or another local process's requests from spending the allowance. None exists: the limiter key is the socket address and no origin check covers ceremony routes. Simple cross-site POSTs are sent by browsers without a preflight. Confidence stays medium for the localhost demo.

T-004: Challenged: the scenario fails if IDs are unguessable and never reused, or if admins never delete their accounts. Neither is stated; CF-001 shows the specs disagree on admin self-deletion, and FR-7.5 lets one admin delete another. Confidence stays medium until an ID rule exists.
T-005: Sought a statement limiting bearer tokens to link routes; found only indirect support (FR-5.2, data flows 5 and 6, SC-014). Controls examined: CTL-SC-014.

T-006: Compared single-object routes with the admin list-all path and with token access; SC-016 covers every read, edit and delete in one module. Controls examined: CTL-SC-016, CTL-SC-021, CTL-SC-002.
T-007: Checked the admin list, dialogs and tooltip contexts against SC-009 and SC-010; both apply to every view. Uploads and previews do not exist. Controls examined: CTL-SC-009, CTL-SC-010.
T-008: Sought any rule on embedded credentials, host display form or title characters; none found. Controls examined: CTL-SC-003, CTL-SC-009.
T-009: Counter-evidence is the localhost-only deployment and admin deletion. The premise holds only if hosted.
T-010: Sought a normalization rule for the own-host comparison; none found. Controls examined: CTL-SC-003.
T-011: Sought a limit that applies when the token is unknown or missing, and any bound on event volume; none found. Controls examined: CTL-SC-018, CTL-SC-025.

T-012: Challenged and narrowed: click-count inflation is behavior the owner accepted in FR-3.7, so it is not treated as a defect. The availability effect remains: unlimited anonymous requests each cause a synchronous write in a single process. CF-002 notes that SC-015's 'no GET changes state' wording does not hold for this route.
T-013: Counter-evidence is the size of the code space. The remaining premise is the random source (G-015). Controls examined: CTL-SC-020.

T-014: Challenged: a single synchronous process makes interleaving unlikely within one transaction, and SEC-052's rolled_back outcome implies one. The specs still do not require it, and DR-5 splits the work across two modules. Stays open at low confidence.

T-015: Challenged: registration needs a user gesture and, under SC-011, user verification on the new authenticator, but that verifies the intruder's authenticator, not the account owner. The event file records the addition but only the operator reads it. Nothing lets the owner detect or undo it. Confidence stays medium.
T-016: No shared cache, other tenant or account switch exists; the only recipient mismatch is a later user of the same browser profile. Controls examined: CTL-SC-020, CTL-SC-014.
T-017: The specs disclose each localhost assumption; no rule forces a review before hosting. Controls examined: CTL-SC-013, CTL-SC-010.

Rely on SameSite alone (rejected by SC-015's own sources)

treatments.outcome: Ceremony routes get the same origin and content-type gate as authenticated routes, and a challenge can be completed only by the browser that requested it, exactly once.
alternatives: Bind the challenge through a short-lived pre-session cookie
Return an opaque ceremony ID that the same page must present
Leave ceremony routes ungated and rely on WebAuthn origin checks only

Atomic consumption means a failed verify forces a fresh challenge

treatments.outcome: Requests from other origins, or addressed to another host name, are refused before they count against the sign-up and login allowance, so another page cannot spend the user's attempts.
alternatives: Key the limit on something a cross-site page cannot share (not available without storing visitor data)
Accept the lockout risk for a single-user localhost demo
tradeoffs: Local processes on the same host can still spend the allowance; that is inherent to an address key on loopback

treatments.outcome: An internal user ID is unguessable, is never issued twice, and an admin-list entry that matches no current user is reported at startup, so admin authority cannot pass to a later sign-up.
alternatives: Identify admins by a passkey credential instead of a user ID
Remove deleted admins from configuration by procedure only
tradeoffs: Random IDs are longer to copy into configuration
A startup warning depends on the operator reading the event file

treatments.outcome: Each route accepts exactly one kind of credential. Bearer tokens work only on the link operations of FR-5.2; account, passkey, token-management and admin routes accept only a session; a request carrying both is refused.
alternatives: Scoped tokens with per-token permissions (more than the demo needs)
Allow tokens on admin routes for admin users
tradeoffs: Admin automation by token is not possible
Clients must not send cookies with token calls

treatments.outcome: Every link operation binds the caller, the link's owner and the action in the Links module, and every admin operation checks the configured role, whichever credential is used. Keep SC-016 and SC-021 and prove them per operation.
alternatives: Check ownership in each route (rejected by DR-2)
tradeoffs: None beyond test effort

treatments.outcome: User-supplied titles and URLs stay inert text in every view, including the admin list, confirmation dialogs and tooltips. Keep SC-009 and SC-010 and prove them in the privileged views.
alternatives: Server-side stripping of markup (not needed if rendering is inert)
tradeoffs: None beyond test effort

treatments.outcome: What is stored and shown for a target is the parsed, normalized URL, so the visible host is the real destination. Targets with embedded credentials are refused, and titles cannot carry control or direction-override characters.
alternatives: Show a warning badge on unusual URLs instead of refusing them
Strip, rather than refuse, embedded credentials and control characters
tradeoffs: A few legitimate URLs with embedded credentials are refused
Internationalized hosts appear in their encoded form, which is less readable

treatments.outcome: Before the system is reachable by anyone outside the team, the owner decides how sign-up and link targets are constrained (for example invitations, a warning page before leaving, or an allow-list). Until then the system stays on localhost.
alternatives: Invite-only sign-up
Interstitial page before redirecting
Target domain allow-list
Accept the abuse risk and rely on admin deletion
tradeoffs: Each option changes FR-1.5 or FR-3.1, which the owner set deliberately

treatments.outcome: The own-domain rule compares normalized host names and treats every name for the local machine as the site itself while the site runs on localhost, so a link cannot point back at the service.
alternatives: Detect loops at redirect time instead
Compare full origins (host and port) only
tradeoffs: Links to other services on the developer's own machine are refused in the demo

treatments.outcome: API calls that present no valid token share the address-keyed allowance used for login, and each kind of denial event has a per-minute ceiling with a count of suppressed events, so an anonymous caller can neither bypass the limit nor flush audit evidence quickly.
alternatives: Write audit-required events to a separate file with its own retention (needs an owner decision on OD-004/OD-005)
Stop emitting an event per unknown token
tradeoffs: Bursts of genuine denials lose per-event detail beyond the ceiling
The address key shares the loopback weakness described in T-003

treatments.outcome: The owner decides whether unlimited anonymous redirects, each with a synchronous write, are acceptable for the demo or whether the write cost per request must be bounded. Click-count inflation stays accepted under FR-3.7.
alternatives: Accept for the localhost demo
Bound redirect load without storing visitor data (a global ceiling)
Decouple counting from the request path
tradeoffs: A global ceiling can refuse genuine visitors during a flood and changes NFR-1.3
Decoupled counting can lose counts on a crash

treatments.outcome: Short codes are drawn from a cryptographic random source with every character equally likely, so codes cannot be predicted from earlier ones.
alternatives: Longer codes (changes FR-2.7)
tradeoffs: None

treatments.outcome: Deleting an account removes or revokes the user, passkeys, sessions, tokens and links as one all-or-nothing change, and a request that started before the deletion cannot act for the account after it.
alternatives: Ordered steps with compensating cleanup at startup
tradeoffs: Auth and Links must share one transaction while keeping DR-3 and DR-4 ownership

treatments.outcome: The owner decides how an account holder can detect and undo an unwanted passkey, and whether adding a passkey, creating a token or deleting the account needs a fresh passkey check.
alternatives: List and remove passkeys on the account page
Require a fresh passkey assertion before sensitive account actions
Both
Accept for the demo; the event file is the only record
tradeoffs: Passkey removal needs a rule against removing the last passkey (FR-1.8)
Fresh checks add a prompt to each sensitive action

treatments.outcome: Authenticated responses, above all the one-time token, are never stored by the browser, so nothing remains readable after sign-out.
alternatives: Mark only the token response
tradeoffs: Slightly more network traffic; negligible at this scale

treatments.outcome: The localhost-only decisions are named in one place and block any other deployment until the owner has decided transport security, proxy trust, the rate-limit key and exposure of open sign-up.
alternatives: Fail startup when the configured origin is not localhost
Document only

treatments.outcome: Suppression applies only to records with no identified actor. A denial or failure by a signed-in user or a valid token is always written, so an identified caller cannot hide their own actions, and anonymous noise cannot hide them either.
alternatives: Separate ceilings per event name and reason code
Always write the first record per actor per minute and count the rest per actor
Write audit and denial events to separate files (DEC-006)

verification.approach: With a test session, send each non-GET route a request marked cross-site, one with a null origin and one with a non-JSON content type; then send the same request as the SPA would. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: Cross-site and non-JSON requests are refused with no state change; the same-origin JSON request succeeds.
verification.pass_criteria: Every non-GET cookie route refuses all three hostile variants and state is unchanged; the legitimate request succeeds.
verification.fail_criteria: Any hostile variant changes state on any route.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: A route is untested, or state before and after was not observed.

verification.approach: Request options in one browser context and try to complete the ceremony from another context and from a cross-site page; submit the same completion twice at once. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: Only the requesting context completes the ceremony, and only once.
verification.pass_criteria: Completion from another context or cross-site is refused, and of two simultaneous completions at most one succeeds.
verification.fail_criteria: A session is created for a context that did not request the challenge, or both simultaneous completions succeed.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: Challenge storage or session creation was not observable.

verification.approach: From a cross-site page context, send more than the allowed number of ceremony requests in a minute, then attempt a normal login from the application. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: The cross-site requests are refused without consuming the allowance; the normal login is not rate-limited.
verification.pass_criteria: The legitimate login proceeds after the cross-site burst.
verification.fail_criteria: The legitimate login receives a rate-limit refusal caused by the cross-site burst.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: The limiter's count was not observable or the burst did not reach the server.

verification.approach: Create an account, list its ID as admin, delete the account, then sign up new accounts and inspect their IDs and role; restart with the stale ID still configured. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: No new account ever receives the deleted ID or admin authority; startup reports one unmatched admin entry.
verification.pass_criteria: New accounts get fresh IDs and no admin access; the unmatched entry is reported by count.
verification.fail_criteria: A new account receives a previously used ID or admin access.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: ID generation could not be exercised enough to observe reuse behavior, or startup events were not captured.

verification.approach: From supplied policy, write a matrix of route by credential type (session, token, both, none) marked allowed or denied; call every route with each credential type using a normal and an admin test account. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: Only the cells marked allowed succeed.
verification.pass_criteria: Every observed cell matches the matrix; token calls to account, token and admin routes are refused; requests with both credentials are refused.
verification.fail_criteria: A token reaches a non-link route, or a request with both credentials is acted on.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: A route or credential type is missing from the matrix or untested.

verification.approach: With two ordinary test accounts and one admin, each owning known links, write the expected matrix of actor by link by action (view, edit, delete, admin list, admin delete, admin user delete) from FR-4 and FR-7; exercise every cell by cookie and by token. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: Cross-owner cells return the same not-found as a random code and leave the link unchanged; non-admin calls to admin routes are refused; responses contain only allowed fields.
verification.pass_criteria: Every observed cell matches the matrix.
verification.fail_criteria: Any cross-owner read or change, any admin action by a non-admin, or any response field outside the schema.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: A cell was not exercised or the link's state afterwards was not observed.

verification.approach: Create links whose titles and targets contain markup and script-like text; view them as the owner and as an admin in the list, the delete dialog and the tooltip. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: The text appears literally and nothing executes; no anchor points at a target URL.
verification.pass_criteria: All views show literal text, no script runs, and the page's markup contains no link to a target.
verification.fail_criteria: Any view interprets the content or renders a live link to a target.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: A view (for example the admin delete dialog) was not checked.

verification.approach: Submit targets with a trusted-looking name before an @ sign and with an internationalized look-alike host, and titles with direction-override and control characters; view the results in the list and the delete dialog. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: Credential-bearing targets and control-character titles are refused with a reason; an internationalized host is displayed in its encoded form.
verification.pass_criteria: All refusals occur and the displayed host always equals the redirect's real host.
verification.fail_criteria: A deceptive form is accepted, or the displayed host differs from the real destination.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: Display in one of the views was not observed.

verification.approach: Review of the deployment plan: confirm the decision is recorded before any non-localhost origin is configured. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: A recorded owner decision exists before hosting.
verification.pass_criteria: The decision record exists and the specs reflect it.
verification.fail_criteria: The system is configured with a non-localhost origin with no decision recorded.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: No deployment plan exists to review.

verification.approach: Submit targets that name the service by alternate loopback spellings, a trailing dot, different letter case and another port; then submit an ordinary external target. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: All self-referencing forms are refused with the FR-2.10 reason; the external target is accepted.
verification.pass_criteria: Every alternate form is refused and the external target is accepted.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: The configured site host used in the test is unknown.

verification.approach: Send a burst of API calls, each with a different random token, well above the per-minute allowance; then count the refusals and the events written. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: Calls beyond the allowance are refused as rate-limited; the number of rejection events stays at the ceiling and a suppressed count is reported.
verification.pass_criteria: Refusals begin at the allowance and event volume is bounded with a reported suppressed count.
verification.fail_criteria: All calls are processed, or one event is written per call without bound.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: The event file or limiter state was not observable.

verification.approach: In an isolated setup, apply a sustained high rate of redirect requests while timing an authenticated API call. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: The API stays responsive within a limit the owner sets, or the owner has recorded acceptance.
verification.pass_criteria: Responsiveness meets the owner's stated limit under the test load.
verification.fail_criteria: The API becomes unresponsive under the test load and no acceptance is recorded.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: No limit or acceptance has been stated, or load could not be generated safely.

verification.approach: Review the generation code path and sample a large batch of generated codes for character distribution. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: The source is the platform's cryptographic generator and the selection is unbiased.
verification.pass_criteria: Code review confirms the source and the sample shows no bias beyond chance.
verification.fail_criteria: A non-cryptographic source or biased mapping is used.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: The code path was not reviewed.

verification.approach: Force a store failure midway through an account deletion; then check the account, its links, tokens and sessions. Repeat without the failure and try the old token and session. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: After a forced failure everything is as before; after success nothing of the account works.
verification.pass_criteria: The failed deletion leaves all records intact and reports rolled_back; the successful one leaves no working link, token or session.
verification.fail_criteria: Any partial state survives, or an old credential works after deletion.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: The failure could not be injected or the resulting state was not inspected.

verification.approach: With a test account, add a second passkey from an existing session and check what the owner can see and undo, and whether a fresh check was demanded. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: Behavior matches the owner's recorded decision.
verification.pass_criteria: The observed behavior matches the decision.
verification.fail_criteria: The observed behavior contradicts the decision.

verification.approach: Inspect the cache directive on every API response and, after logout, use browser back navigation to the token and list screens. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: Every API response forbids storage; after logout no earlier data is shown.
verification.pass_criteria: All API responses carry the no-storage directive and no data reappears after logout.
verification.fail_criteria: Any authenticated response is storable or reappears after logout.

verification.approach: Start the server with a non-localhost origin configured. Run only in an isolated test setup with synthetic accounts, when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: Startup is refused, or a recorded owner decision covers the hosted design.
verification.pass_criteria: Startup fails closed or the decision record exists.
verification.fail_criteria: The server starts on a non-localhost origin with the demo settings and no decision.

verification.approach: In an isolated setup, send 200 anonymous rejected requests in a minute, then one cross-owner request from a signed-in test user, and read the event file. Run only when the caller authorizes it.
verification.expected_outcome: The signed-in user's denial is written in full even though the anonymous ceiling was reached.
verification.pass_criteria: The identified denial record is present with its actor reference, and the suppressed count covers only anonymous records.
verification.fail_criteria: The identified denial is missing from the file.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: The event file was not captured or the ceiling was not reached.

decisions.rationale: Proposed for the owner's approval, not applied: rate each risk on impact (low: one user's convenience; medium: one user's data or the service's availability; high: any user's account or admin authority) and on how many preconditions the specs leave open (few, some, many). No rating was calculated from this scale.
A proposed default now answers OD-008: localhost only (NFR-1.4, SC-032). The caller asked for a best answer but has not stated acceptance (E-047).
A proposed default now answers OD-009: passkey list and removal plus a 5-minute re-verification window (FR-1.13 to FR-1.15, SC-033). Awaiting the owner (E-047).
A proposed default now answers OD-010: unlimited redirect load accepted for the demo, one statement per redirect (NFR-1.5, SC-034). Awaiting the owner (E-047).
A proposed default now answers OD-011: an admin cannot delete their own account by any route (FR-7.10). Awaiting the owner (E-047).
Awaiting the owner (optional alternative): whether audit-required events should go to a separate file with their own retention, which would change OD-004 and OD-005.
